items.title: What do the base and index say?
items.student: Notation: a^n means a raised to the power n, not a×n. Write repeated multiplication and evaluate:2^5;3^3;(−2)^4;−2^4. Write 64 as a power of 2 and 81 as a power of 3. Express 72 as a product of prime powers and explain why its expression is not a single prime power. Fictional counters are arranged in 4 groups, each with 4 rows of 4: write the total compactly. Use only the supplied numbers, not anyone’s height or weight.
items.teacher: 2^5=32;3^3=27;(−2)^4=16;−2^4=−16 because the exponent applies to 2 before the leading minus.64=2^6;81=3^4;72=2^3×3^2, two distinct prime factors so not one prime power.4×4×4=4^3=64. Base is the repeated factor; index counts factors for positive whole-number indices. The zero case needs a separate definition/reason, not zero factors multiplied by a literal 0.

items.title: Derive the same-base product law
items.student: Expand and simplify 2^3×2^4;3^2×3^3;5^1×5^2. Count factors before stating a general product rule. Critique claims: A2^3×2^4=2^12; B2^3+2^4=2^7; C2^3×3^4=6^7. State what must match before combining exponents. Work in a group with reader,factor-recorder,checker and reporter; rotate so each person explains a result individually.
items.teacher: Results 2^7=128;3^5=243;5^3=125. Positive exponents count m factors plus n factors, giving a^m×a^n=a^(m+n). The unit’s general statements use nonzero real base a and whole-number exponents; the zero-exponent case is justified later. A confuses product with power-of-a-power;8×16=128, not 4096. B8+16=24, not 128; the law is for multiplication. C8×81=648, not 6^7=279936; the bases differ. Group roles support shared work, but collect an individual explanation rather than infer mastery from the reporter.

items.title: What cancels in a quotient?
items.student: Use repeated factors and cancellation to simplify 2^7÷2^3;5^4÷5^2;3^3÷3^1. State the same-base quotient rule when the base is nonzero and m≥n. Explain why division by 0 cannot be allowed. Optional consequence, not a separate required rule in this unit: expand 2^2÷2^5 and write the result as a fraction. Do not cancel factors across addition.
items.teacher: 2^4=16;5^2=25;3^2=9. Cancellation leaves m−n factors, so a^m/a^n=a^(m−n),a≠0, with m≥n in core practice. For n>m the expanded example 4/32=1/8; a negative-exponent notation can be introduced as an optional consequence, not assumed as prerequisite or required by the final task. The m=n case gives 1 for nonzero base and motivates a^0. Denominators cannot be zero;0/0 has no unique quotient.

items.title: A power of a power counts groups of factors
items.student: Expand(2^3)^2;(3^2)^3;(5^1)^4. Explain why the exponent is multiplied rather than added. Compare(2^3)^2 with 2^3×2^2. Correct the claim(4^2)^3=4^5. Draw a grouping diagram or use repeated multiplication; a calculator display alone is not the explanation.
items.teacher: (2^3)^2=2^6=64;(3^2)^3=3^6=729;(5^1)^4=5^4=625. There are n groups each containing m factors, hence(a^m)^n=a^(mn).2^3×2^2=2^5=32, a different expression. Correct(4^2)^3=4^6=4096, not 4^5=1024. This is repeated multiplication of powers, not a sum of two groups. Use nonzero base in the combined rule sheet to keep zero-exponent domain consistent.

items.title: Why does a nonzero base to power zero equal one?
items.student: Write two evaluations of 7^3÷7^3: one by ordinary division and one using the quotient pattern. Explain the value that 7^0 must have to keep the rules consistent. Evaluate 9^0;(−4)^0;0^3. A claim says “Every base to power 0 equals 1, so 0^0=1 here.” Explain why that argument is invalid. This unit does not assign a value to 0^0.
items.teacher: 343/343=1 and 7^(3−3)=7^0, so the consistent definition is a^0=1 for a≠0.9^0=1 and(−4)^0=1;0^3=0 by ordinary repeated multiplication. The derivation cannot start with 0^3/0^3, because 0/0 is not defined. No value of 0^0 is assigned in this school unit; do not generalise beyond the nonzero domain or assert there is no other mathematical context for the notation.

items.title: Use indices without inventing a real-world pattern
items.student: Fictional stock plan:A each box holds 2^4 beads and 2^3 boxes fit a carton. Find beads per carton in index and ordinary form. B each rack has 3^2 trays and 3^2 objects per tray. Find the total. C a fictional population count is 71,600: round to the nearest thousand, then express the rounded number as a whole-number multiple of 10^3. State that rounding loses detail. D a pattern starts with 3 counters and triples at each stage; stage 0 has 3. Find stages 1,2,3 and a formula for stage n under this stated ideal rule. Do not assume real populations grow by that pattern.
items.teacher: A2^7=128. B3^4=81. C72,000=72×10^3, not an exact restatement of 71,600;10^3=1000. This is index notation, not a requirement that the coefficient be between 1 and 10. D9,27,81;3×3^n=3^(n+1) for whole n≥0. The rule is stipulated, not inferred from two observations or asserted about biological populations. Keep stage number and starting multiplier distinct.

items.title: Audit a four-law reference sheet
items.student: Create a four-law sheet with one derived numerical example for product,quotient,power-of-a-power and zero exponent. State base restrictions and distinguish multiplication from addition. Audit this model:8 shelves,each with 8 boxes,each containing 8 items; another identical store is added. Which expression gives the new total:8^4,2×8^3,or 8^3+2? Explain. Add a reason indices help computation and an individual next learning action. Optional teacher-approved digital verification: open OpenStax Prealgebra 2 e Chapter 10 Key Concepts, https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/10-key-concepts (checked 13 November 2026),locate one of these four laws,record the title/URL and its condition,and compare with your example. Ignore additional properties beyond this unit. Printed law summary:for nonzero a and whole m,n,a^m×a^n=a^(m+n);a^m÷a^n=a^(m−n) when m≥n;(a^m)^n=a^(mn);a^0=1. All learners retain this printed route.
items.teacher: One store 8^3=512;two stores 2×8^3=1024,not 8^4=4096 or 514. The base counts repeated factors only where the model says so. Require an individual derivation/check in addition to the group sheet. Rotate leadership/checking roles; observe respectful participation separately. For digital use precheck the official page/cached copy and allocate up to 4 minutes of the 16-minute task slot only when access/observation is feasible. Record each learner’s navigation/title/URL/condition comparison as independent,prompted or not observed; print-only work does not demonstrate digital navigation/responsible handling. No personal data entry or unrelated links. If devices are unavailable plan an accessible later station before claiming digital competence. The printed summary is an authored mathematical reference; it is not quoted curriculum wording.

items.title: Independent index-notation data
items.student: Notation:a^n means a raised to power n. All bases in the required law computations are nonzero and all input exponents are whole numbers. Fictional design:A a crate contains 5^3 packets,each packet holds 5^2 tiles. B a separate count is 48,600,which must be reported to the nearest thousand. C a store has 4 racks,each with 4 shelves and 4 objects per shelf; a second identical store is added. Use these data and the separate task prompts only. Calculators may check completed working; they do not replace expanded-factor explanations.
items.teacher: Release only with Lesson 8 assessment prompts. A5^5=3125; B49,000=49×10^3; C2×4^3=128. Final law examples are 3^2×3^4=3^6=729;2^8÷2^5=2^3=8;(5^2)^2=5^4=625;11^0=1. All worked answers remain in teacher files. No negative-exponent or scientific-notation convention beyond the stated whole-number multiple of 10^3 is required.
